newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
WIESBADEN - The German direct marketing association says its agencies boosted turnover by an average of 10 percent last year, largely driven by business from financial services companies.
(Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Automaker Seat, a unit of Volkswagen AG, is looking for a new lead advertising agency to manage its account from one office. Until now, Seat's account has been held by Spanish agency Casadevall Pedreno in cooperation with the Wilkens network, but VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech has demanded a change. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - A study by the U.S. institute Forrester Research predicts brand-name consumer products manufacturers in three years will be devoting 10 percent of their advertising budgets to online ads -- more than five times the current rate.
(Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Pharmaceutical company Bayer plans to launch a new global image campaign and is accepting pitches from several agencies. The company has been represented internationally until now by Munich-based agency Publicis MCD. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
COLOGNE - Television broadcaster Vox has no plans to become more integrated in the RTL group if that means centralising planning and marketing, Vox president Markus Tellenbach says.

Tellenbach was responsding to a report in the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel that French media group Canal Plus planned to sell its 24.9 percent stake in Vox to CLT/Ufa, Europe's largest broadcaster jointly owned by Bertelsmann and Audiofina.
(Reuter)

BONN - ProSieben Media AG says three additional banks have signed on as underwriters for its share listing, the first of a German television network, that is scheduled for July. ProSieben, whose main shareholders are the Rewe retail group and Thomas Kirch, son of Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, plans to float 17.5 million non-voting preference shares on stock exchanges in July. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German trade publications maintained stable turnover and circulation in 1996 and foresee steady growth for the current year, the German Trade Press Association says. With nearly 3,500 titles and 513 million distributed annually, trade publications made a total 3.9 billion marks last year -- more than half of which came from advertising sales, the association says. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Publishing groups Burda and Holtzbrinck have merged their CD-ROM businesses, Burda says. Burda says the two companies have been working closely together on high-end multimedia products since May 1. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
HERZOGENAURACH - Sportswear manufacturer Adidas AG says its first quarter profits for this year are up 33 percent.
(Reuter)
COLOGNE - Retail group Metro Holding AG says its sales were up in the first quarter of 1997, positively influenced by business at Easter. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Music company Stella AG plans to list 49 percent of its shares this year on the stock exchange, the company says. Industry sources say it would be the first company in Germany that is exclusively in the entertainment business to float shares. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Carmaker Volkswagen AG says its first quarter net profit rose nearly 50 percent and sales increased 10 percent -- mainly abroad due to a slowdown in the German market with help from the dollar. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Stephan Becker-Sonnenschein, marketing communications manager at tobacco company Philip Morris' unit in Munich, has been elected president of the German Publication Relations Society. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Yves Englebert has taken over as advertising sales director of finance magazine Capital. (Kress)
MUNICH - Michael Kaudera has been named managing director of DSF SportMarketing GmbH. (Kress)
